filesRead: docs/工程技术架构与项目结构.md
scope.followupLimit: Re-review ACL001–ACL006 and the related revised contracts/example only; no new architecture review.
scope.method: Read frozen revised candidate documents and hashes. Reason through the same counterexamples against the revised text; no runtime or compiled verification.

findings.evidence: A dedicated cross-host cancellation section now defines DOM-free CancellationSignal with aborted, reason, addEventListener and removeEventListener; once-only abort, stable reason, already-aborted behavior, operation pre/post registration checks and exception-contained notification are explicit. Browser compatibility is correctly left to later real type checks rather than asserted as compiled.
findings.remainingValidation: Implement and compile the portable signature and browser/mini-game adapters; then validate cancellation races and throwing listeners.

findings.evidence: Closing/closed use now distinguishes same-Scope registered values, foreign-owned values and fresh unowned late results. Same-Scope values are rejected without early cleanup, so the lease-first/Bitmap-second reverse order survives abort callback reentry. Notification and diagnostics exceptions cannot block cleanup completion.
findings.remainingValidation: Implement owner bookkeeping and validate abort callback reentry with both same-owner and new late values.

findings.evidence: Recursive disposal carries the initiating root owner boundary, including an explicit unowned-root rule. An unowned intermediate container does not change that boundary. Foreign-owned children detach and stop recursion into their subtree; sibling and root cleanup continue after failures.
findings.remainingValidation: Validate nested owned/unowned trees and error continuation after implementation.

findings.evidence: The whole dispatch freezes all node/phase candidates at its start; target capture/non-capture groups, finite integer priority/default, stop flags, descriptor defaults, capture for non-bubbling tree events and active Event redispatch rejection are now stated. The same cross-phase listener-addition and once reentry counterexamples have a consistent specified outcome.
findings.remainingValidation: Implement dispatch and verify mutation, stop flags, errors and nested new-event dispatch against own behavior cases; legacy matching remains separate.

findings.evidence: Objects bind to an Engine through Scope registration or first mount, detach retains binding, and cross-Engine mount/adoption/resource binding rejects. Shared source assets require separate instance acquire. Surface ownership is exclusive by default; explicitly tested host sharing is an exception, and a borrowed-device host owner arbitrates submission, epoch and lifetime.
findings.remainingValidation: Validate binding atomicity, conflicting surface acquisition and borrowed-device arbitration across real adapters.

findings.evidence: Engine.dispose now creates one close Promise shared by reentrant/repeated callers, preserving a failed result without implicit retry. Bounded cleanup failures reject with diagnostics and prohibit reuse; in-flight handles are retained until completion. EgretError cause plus readonly cleanupErrors preserve the original operation failure in the revised catch example.
findings.remainingValidation: Compile the public error constructor and sample, then validate shutdown failure, timeout, reentry and completion retention.

nonBlockingNotes: Initial cross-Scope ownership transfer is explicitly unavailable, which removes the undefined transfer promise without expanding the API.
Bitmap Texture borrowing still requires the creator to retain its lease until all borrowers stop; no implicit per-Bitmap lease or proof of per-lease misuse detection has been introduced.
conclusion: All six initial document-level corrections are resolved in the frozen hashes reviewed. This verdict is restricted to internal consistency of those candidate contracts and example; it does not accept D016, prove compatibility/performance, or claim implementation, compilation, tests or CI pass.
